theme: Chance rates of Parpola's rebus homophones and compound interlocks in Dravidian and comparison lexicons
question: How often does Parpola's homophone procedure find a picture-to-name homophone in each candidate language, and how often do his Tamil compound interlocks appear when the words he started from are replaced by random words of the same productivity and frequency?
outcome: In the Tamil Lexicon, compounds muruku-X and X-mīṉ share a member for 30.5% of 2,500 random replacement pairs (95% bootstrap 25.2-36.2%; 40.3% and 28.7% for pools of 25 and 100; 52.8% under the practised stem tolerance), so the frozen rule kills the veḷ interlock as evidence (threshold 20%). Four of five encoded interlocks hold for Parpola's words (veḷ, vaṭa-mīṉ, numeral-mīṉ compounds, katir-k-kaṭavuḷ; Muruka-p-piḷḷai is not in the Lexicon), and all four hold together in 0.44% of 10,000 random draws (2.2% under the practised tolerance), so the network passes the frozen 1% rule. Single homophones between 751 picturable nouns and 436 name meanings occur for 2.31% of evaluable pairs in DEDR, 1.50% in Turner's CDIAL and 0.45% in ePSD2; the Dravidian rate is 2.37 times the median and fails the frozen band of 0.5-2. Restricting each Tamil word to its own gloss lowers the Dravidian rate to 0.29%. Post-outcome: at Parpola's narrower search depth the veḷ link has a 7.8% chance rate; four successes among templates with mean chance rate 0.21 become likely once about 17 templates are tried; mīṉ forms star compounds with three, five, six and seven but not with two.
challenge: DEDR and Turner carry all-rights-reserved notices and the Tamil Lexicon edition CC BY-NC-ND 2.0, so all raw and derived lexical data stay local. No machine-readable Munda or Burushaski dictionary was found; those languages enter as wordlists of 113 and 204 concepts. Concept matching depends on each dictionary's English gloss style. The interlock reruns use one Tamil dictionary of 1924-1936. The network's rarity depends on how many templates Parpola examined, which is unknown. The frozen restricted search missed muruka-vēḷ because the Lexicon glosses it by cross-reference.
remedy: Logged every request with URL, bytes, SHA-256 and time and rebuilt the manifest from disk hashes after concurrent log appends lost 15 lines. Streamed the 1.9 GB ePSD2 glossary. Repaired DEDR, Tamil Lexicon, Lexibank and Munda parsing before the freeze. A synthetic selftest checked Parpola's own pairs, planted homophones and interlocks, and matched the shared-member null to its hypergeometric value. An independent reimplementation found a vowel-set defect (y treated as a vowel) after the freeze; Amendment 1 repaired it, kept results-v1 and recomputed results-v2, and all seven verification checks then agreed. Post-outcome analyses are in a separate labelled output.
retry_when: A blind list of at least 20 Indus sign pairs with Parpola's 1994 picture identifications, frozen before any Tamil compound is looked up; a second Tamil dictionary with compounds (Winslow 1862 or Kadirvelu Pillai on DSAL); or a machine-readable Munda or Burushaski dictionary. Rerunning the same search on the Madras Tamil Lexicon adds nothing.
